goal: Close the selftest --team loop so it fails for an unlisted or requireTeam-less work command
spec: REVIEWER FAIL on task 002, finding is real: the loop at ~line 985 iterates a hand-typed list, so an unlisted command falls to default: die(usage), whose text contains --team and exits nonzero => false pass. Proven by adding 'case purge: requireTeam()

1) Derive the work-command set from the source of main() itself (the case labels in its switch), not from a hand-typed literal. Exclude the non-work commands team and selftest. A regex over the file text is enough
2) Assert every derived work case actually calls requireTeam() — so a new 'case purge:' that omits requireTeam() fails selftest.
3) Spawn each derived command with no --team and assert exit nonzero AND /--team/ in stderr, as now.

4) Add a negative self-check inside selftest: if a case labelled 'purge' that never calls requireTeam() were present, the derived-set assertion must fail. Simulate it in the sandbox or assert the derivation returns the expected count
do not leave a live bogus case.
5) Keep selftest under ~2s of added runtime.
6) done --note must state the real count of work commands, not an estimate.
